questions.q: What happened to Abijah the son of Jeroboam?
questions.a: Abijah the son of Jeroboam fell sick.

questions.q: What did Jeroboam ask his wife to do?
questions.a: Jeroboam asked his wife to disguise herself and go to the prophet Ahijah in Shiloh.

questions.q: Why did Jeroboam ask his wife to go to the prophet Ahijah?
questions.a: Jeroboam asked his wife to go to the prophet Ahijah to find out what would happen to his sick son.

questions.q: What was wrong with Ahijah’s eyes?
questions.a: Since Ahijah was old, he was blind and his eyes could not see.

questions.q: Who told Ahijah, “The wife of Jeroboam is coming to see you.”?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ahijah, “The wife of Jeroboam is coming to see you to seek advice concerning her son.”

questions.q: What did Ahijah say to the wife of Jeroboam?
questions.a: When Ahijah heard her come in at the door he said to her, “I know you are Jeroboam’s wife, so do not pretend that you are someone else.”

questions.q: What did the God of Israel say about Jeroboam?
questions.a: The God of Israel said to Jeroboam, “You are not like my servant David, who kept my commandments.”

questions.q: What did Jeroboam do to provoke Yahweh to anger?
questions.a: Jeroboam cast metal images to provoke Yahweh to anger.

questions.q: What disaster would Yahweh bring on Jeroboam?
questions.a: Yahweh said that he would cut off from him every male of his household, whether they are family members or servants, whether they are young or old.

questions.q: What would happen to anyone of Jeroboam’s family who died in the city?
questions.a: Any of Jeroboam’s family who died in the city would be eaten by dogs.

questions.q: What would all Israel do for the child of Jeroboam?
questions.a: All Israel would mourn for and bury the child of Jeroboam.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say that Jeroboam led Israel to do?
questions.a: Yahweh said that Jeroboam led Israel to worship statues of the goddess Asherah, as he was doing.

questions.q: How far did Yahweh say that he would scatter Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh said that he would scatter Israel beyond the Euphrates River.

questions.q: What happened when Jeroboam’s wife came to the threshold of the house?
questions.a: When Jeroboam’s wife came to the threshold of the house, the child died.

questions.q: What did all Israel do after the child died?
questions.a: All Israel buried him and mourned for him.

questions.q: Where were the other matters concerning Jeroboam written?
questions.a: The other matters concerning Jeroboam were written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel.

questions.q: How many years did Jeroboam reign before he slept with his fathers?
questions.a: Jeroboam reigned for 22 years, and he slept with his fathers.

questions.q: Who was reigning in Judah?
questions.a: Rehoboam the son of Solomon was reigning in Judah.

questions.q: How did Judah provoke Yahweh to jealousy?
questions.a: Judah provoked Yahweh to jealousy with the sins they committed.

questions.q: What did Judah build on every high hill and under every green tree?
questions.a: Judah built shrines and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.

questions.q: What despicable things did the nations do?
questions.a: The Israelite people did the same disgraceful things with male prostitutes that the people had done whom Yahweh had forced to leave so that the Israelites could possess the land.

questions.q: In what year did Shishak come up against Jerusalem?
questions.a: In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak came up against Jerusalem.

questions.q: What shields did Shishak take away from Jerusalem?
questions.a: Shishak took all the shields of gold that Solomon had made.

questions.q: What did King Rehoboam do with the shields of bronze that he made?
questions.a: King Rehoboam put them into the hands of the palace guards.

questions.q: When would the guards carry the shields of bronze?
questions.a: Whenever the king entered the house of Yahweh, the guards would carry the shields.

questions.q: Where were the other matters of King Rehoboam written?
questions.a: The other matters of King Rehoboam were written in book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah.

questions.q: Who became king in Rehoboam’s place?
questions.a: Abijah, Rehoboam’s son, became king in his place.

commentary.text: Abijah being sick, his mother consults Ahijah.

Verses 1–6 “At that time,” when Jeroboam did evil, his child sickened. When sickness comes into our families, we should inquire whether there may not be some particular sin harboured in our houses, which the affliction is sent to convince us of, and reclaim us from. It had been more pious if he had desired to know wherefore God contended with him; had begged the prophet's prayers, and cast away his idols from him; but most people would rather be told their fortune, than their faults or their duty. He sent to Ahijah, because he had told him he should be king. Those who by sin disqualify themselves for comfort, yet expect that their ministers, because they are good men, should speak peace and comfort to them, greatly wrong themselves and their ministers. He sent his wife in disguise, that the prophet might only answer her question concerning her son. Thus some people would limit their ministers to smooth things, and care not for having the whole counsel of God declared to them, lest it should prophesy no good concerning them, but evil. But she shall know, at the first word, what she has to trust to. Tidings of a portion with hypocrites will be heavy tidings. God will judge men according to what they are, not by what they seem to be.

Whether we keep an account of God's mercies to us or not, he does; and he will set them in order before us, if we are ungrateful, to our greater confusion. Ahijah foretells the speedy death of the child then sick, in mercy to him. He only in the house of Jeroboam had affection for the true worship of God, and disliked the worship of the calves. To show the power and sovereignty of his grace, God saves some out of the worst families, in whom there is some good thing towards the Lord God of Israel. The righteous are removed from the evil to come in this world, to the good to come in a better world. It is often a bad sign for a family, when the best in it are buried out of it. Yet their death never can be a loss to themselves. It was a present affliction to the family and kingdom, by which both ought to have been instructed. God also tells the judgments which should come upon the people of Israel, for conforming to the worship Jeroboam established. After they left the house of David, the government never continued long in one family, but one undermined and destroyed another. Families and kingdoms are ruined by sin. If great men do wickedly, they draw many others, both into the guilt and punishment. The condemnation of those will be severest, who must answer, not only for their own sins, but for sins others have been drawn into, and kept in, by them.

Here is no good said of Rehoboam, and much said to the disadvantage of his subjects. The abounding of the worst crimes, of the worst of the heathen, in Jerusalem, the city the Lord had chosen for his temple and his worship, shows that nothing can mend the hearts of fallen men but the sanctifying grace of the Holy Spirit. On this alone may we depend; for this let us daily pray, in behalf of ourselves and all around us. The splendour of their temple, the pomp of their priesthood, and all the advantages with which their religion was attended, could not prevail to keep them close to it; nothing less than the pouring out the Spirit will keep God's Israel in their allegiance to him. Sin exposes, makes poor, and weakens any people. Shishak, king of Egypt, came and took away the treasures. Sin makes the gold become dim, changes the most fine gold, and turns it into brass.
